properties.name: url
properties.notes: Where the animation was fetched from. Resolved into `json` once, in the builder; the generated widget never reaches the network.

properties.name: json
properties.notes: The Lottie animation itself, as JSON text. This is what is compiled into the Remote Compose document, so it is what the export needs.

properties.name: progress
properties.notes: Pins the animation to one frame, 0 (first) to 1 (last). Unset — the default — lets the document's animation clock run it in a loop.

svg.notes: A placeholder on the canvas must not claim structured SVG parity with an animation.

wasm.notes: Drawn as a named placeholder carrying the animation's source and size. The canvas has no Lottie renderer, and compiling the animation the way the export does — into Remote Compose operations — is Horologist's Android-only creation API, which a Wasm build cannot link. A lookalike would be an impression of an animation nobody could check; the picture comes from the native lane, which builds this design's own generated document.

properties.name: showByState
properties.notes: Select one child by state. Object fields: selector is a typed scalar or state read; cases is an object mapping child IDs to typed scalar values; optional fallback is a string child ID. Every child must be a case or the fallback. Compose export uses when. Remote export uses StateLayout for non-null number or flag selectors; String equality is unavailable on that target.

properties.name: verticalArrangement
properties.notes: Distribution down the axis. The three aligned values compose with verticalSpacingDp through Arrangement.spacedBy(space, alignment); the three space* values distribute the free space themselves, and Compose has no form that also inserts a fixed gap.

properties.name: alignment
properties.notes: How a parent Box aligns this column. The renderer has always read `alignment` off any Box child and the exporter has always emitted `.align(...)` for it; only the declaration was missing, so a centred column was inexpressible.

properties.name: horizontalArrangement
properties.notes: The Row counterpart of a Column’s verticalArrangement, with the same relationship to horizontalSpacingDp.

properties.name: data
properties.notes: The rows: a `list` value whose entries are `object` values — one dictionary per row, read by the template through `{"type":"binding","value":"<key>"}`, the same reader a component body uses for its arguments.

svg.notes: Repeated rows draw the template more than once, and the structured recorder correlates a text element by authored node id — so only the last row's measurements survive and the typography annotation cannot be matched. Unverified until the recorder reads instance paths, which makes an SVG export of a design holding a loop refuse by name rather than emit an unannotated one.

properties.name: horizontalArrangement
properties.notes: Distribution along a line, exactly as on layout/row, and composing with horizontalSpacingDp the same way.

properties.name: verticalArrangement
properties.notes: Distribution of the LINES, not of the children: a flow row's cross axis is the stack of rows it wrapped into, so this is a Column's vocabulary and verticalSpacingDp is the gap between lines.

properties.name: maxItemsInEachRow
properties.notes: A ceiling on the children one line may hold, for a design that wants a fixed number per row however much space there is. Absent means as many as fit, which is the reason to reach for this component at all.

properties.name: alignment
properties.notes: How a parent Box aligns this flow row, read off any Box child exactly as on layout/column.

wasm.notes: RemoteFlowRow. Not in the Glance Wear widget profile (LAYOUT_FLOW): the Native / Live render of a widget using it fails while the document is captured.

properties.name: horizontalAlignment
properties.notes: Where the chosen child sits across the box. Centred when absent.

properties.name: verticalArrangement
properties.notes: Where the chosen child sits down the box. Centred when absent.

wasm.notes: RemoteFitBox: its children are alternatives, largest first, and it shows the first one that fits.

properties.name: verticalArrangement

properties.name: color
properties.notes: A colour, written as {"type":"color","value":"#RRGGBB"} or as {"type":"colorToken","value":"primary"} naming one of statusSemantics.colorTokens. A string wrapper, or a role the canvas does not draw, is refused at commit.

svg.notes: The pinned same-runtime recorder retains text; font embedding and Figma text metrics remain a separate release gate.

wasm.notes: Fidelity requires the pinned Jetcaster font assets and typography tokens.

properties.name: documentBase64
properties.notes: Base64-encoded Remote Compose wire document; limited to 8 MiB encoded. Not required on its own: a node carries either the bytes or a documentUrl, and the editor's own rule reports a node that carries neither.

properties.name: documentUrl
properties.notes: Absolute http(s) URL the host resolves to the same wire document. Read only when documentBase64 is empty, so a design that carries its own bytes never depends on the network.

properties.name: namedValues
properties.notes: Typed host values keyed by the Remote Compose named-variable name.

svg.notes: Nested Remote Compose SVG export requires an explicit renderer implementation.

wasm.notes: Uses the common CMP player. Each named UI Builder slot registers the matching Remote Compose custom-component config.

properties.name: name
properties.notes: The custom-component config name the document writes and the host registers a renderer under. Namespaced by convention (slot:, rc:, or an application domain) so two documents composed together cannot collide.

properties.name: widthDp
properties.notes: The bounds the document reserves for host content it cannot measure. A player lays out a custom component from the document, not from the Compose content filling it.

svg.notes: Host content inside a Remote Compose document has no structured SVG answer.

wasm.notes: Draws the ordinary Compose content in its own slot, which is what a registered renderer draws on a real player too. A preview only draws it if a custom component of this name is registered; an unregistered one is a player support issue rather than silently borrowed content. The code mapping names the registry rather than a composable, because the composable is whatever the host registers under this name.

properties.name: startColor
properties.notes: A colour, written as {"type":"color","value":"#RRGGBB"} or as {"type":"colorToken","value":"primary"} naming one of statusSemantics.colorTokens. A string wrapper, or a role the canvas does not draw, is refused at commit.

properties.name: endColor
properties.notes: A colour, written as {"type":"color","value":"#RRGGBB"} or as {"type":"colorToken","value":"primary"} naming one of statusSemantics.colorTokens. A string wrapper, or a role the canvas does not draw, is refused at commit.

svg.notes: The frozen benchmark usage records as vector gradient output.

wasm.notes: Must remain a semantic brush layer, not persisted pixel geometry.

properties.name: assetKey
properties.notes: The key of an asset the canvas can draw, written as {"type":"assetKey","value":"…"}: one of statusSemantics.assetRegistry.keys, or a key pinned in the design's own assets map by PUT /api/ui-builder/v1/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetKey} (raw PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP body) or the ui_builder_put_asset MCP tool. Any other key is refused at commit, so put the picture before inserting the node. A pinned key whose bytes this lane cannot show renders as a placeholder naming it, and exports as Image(painter = ColorPainter(...)) with an ASSET_PLACEHOLDER warning.

svg.notes: The recorder embeds the pinned asset bytes, or the project-owned artwork, with source and payload provenance; a key with no bytes behind it is drawn as a vector placeholder rather than declared as a raster fallback.

wasm.notes: Draws the bytes the design's assets map pins under assetKey (content-addressed, hash-checked, stored by the host), the project-owned Jetcaster covers, or a visible placeholder carrying the key. External URLs are not accepted.

adapterStatus.planned: The Compose API is available to Wasm but the catalog authoring adapter is not implemented yet.
adapterStatus.supported: Implemented by the current candidate document renderer.
adapterStatus.unsupported: No verified Wasm execution path exists; documents may retain the node but clean render and export must fail visibly.

assetRegistry.$comment: Every assetKey the catalog itself ships, because these are the assets the canvas draws from its own resources: the two project-owned Jetcaster covers in :ui-builder-artwork, the generated gate-0 cover, and the editor's own insert placeholder. A design extends this set with the keys its assets map pins through the asset lane (PUT /api/ui-builder/v1/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetKey}, ui_builder_put_asset; yschimke/compose-preview-server#478). Both reducers refuse any other key at commit (#484).

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property or a background modifier may name, which are the roles the canvas draws. A colour is otherwise a #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB literal. Mirrored by PropertyValueKinds.CANVAS_COLOR_TOKENS in :ui-builder-export and by the runtime's catalog executor; a test pins the three to this list.

componentMenu.$comment: How the UI builder shelves this catalog in its insert panel. Read by ComponentMenu.from; see ui-builder/src/commonMain/kotlin/ee/schimke/composeai/uibuilder/editor/ComponentMenu.kt. Section names are m3-catalog's own @file:CatalogGroup(section = ...) vocabulary.

svgStatus.raster-fallback-required: The component may export only as a named embedded raster fallback.
svgStatus.unsupported: No honest SVG or declared fallback exists; export must fail.
svgStatus.unverified: The composite SVG spike has not proved this dynamic component; export remains gated.
svgStatus.verified: Proved for this frozen benchmark's authored usage through the pinned same-runtime JVM Skia recorder; this does not verify unused variants or other environments.
